basis: ERIK'S RULING, 2026-09-06 (T3, standing from this run on): where the firm's own claim names NO round and the partnering postdates the company's IPO, the position is not a venture entry and the row is not a member. Redpoint's card says only 'We partnered in 2014' and names no round; Arista Networks IPO'd on the NYSE on 2014-06-06. No Redpoint fund filed a 13D/G or Form 3 on the issuer, and Redpoint Management LLC files 13F-HR from 2022. The same ruling is applied to Accel's arista row in the same pass.

ERIK'S RULING, 2026-09-06 (T3, no round named + partnered after IPO). The card says only 'We first partnered in 2008' and names no round; Internet Brands had been NASDAQ-listed as INET since November 2007. Hellman & Friedman took it private in 2010.

ERIK'S RULING, 2026-09-06 (T3, no round named + partnered after IPO). The card carries no round sentence at all and dates the relationship to 2000; Juniper Networks IPO'd on 1999-06-25 — read 1999-06-25 — four months before Redpoint Ventures I closed. The row was ALSO a decisions.md D5 candidate (in the firm's own 'Previous Investments by Redpoint Partners' table and named in Geoff Yang's IVP bio); T3 settles it independently of the D5 question, which remains open.

ERIK'S RULING, 2026-09-06 (T3, no round named + partnered after IPO). The card carries no round sentence and dates the relationship to 1998; Concur Technologies IPO'd on NASDAQ as CNQR on 1998-12-16, and Redpoint did not exist until October 1999. Like juniper, this row was also a D5 candidate; T3 settles it independently.
